ABS function
notes: The class-numeric argument rule is NEVER checked: IntrinsicSig.ArgKind (the per-position category code, 'n' on the ABS row) has ZERO callers anywhere in src/, and BindArgOperand deliberately routes through BindFunctionArgumentExpr, which skips the 8.8.1.1 class screen for EVERY function (the DA6 comment: an argument's legality comes from its own 15.x rule -- which is then never applied). Failing input: 01 A PIC X(5) VALUE "12345". COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ABS(A) compiles with no diagnostic and yields 12345; likewise FUNCTION ABS("12345"); yet the identical operand in COMPUTE R = A is correctly rejected COBOLNET0844, so the two paths disagree. Table 2 (8.5.2) makes PIC X / an alphanumeric literal / a numeric-edited item CLASS ALPHANUMERIC, so all three violate 15.7.3 r1, and 4.2.2 para 3 requires the violation to be indicated. Converse leak on the same rule: a LEGAL class-numeric argument of float usage (8.5.2.12 item 2) is not supported -- 01 F USAGE COMP-2. COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ABS(F) emits uncompilable C# (CS1503 cannot convert double to System.Int128). No CONFORMANCE-FIX-QUEUE item owns this yet; test-needed.

subject: ABS function
notes: AbsScaled(v) = v < 0 ? -v : v over the unscaled Int128, with the ARGUMENT'S OWN scale carried through by the RenderNum AbsScaled case, is exactly the 15.7.4 equivalent arithmetic expression for both branches, and probes confirm every fixed-point shape: -12.34 -> 12.34, +12.34 -> 12.34, 0 -> 0.00, -7 -> 7, S9(4)PP -1200 -> 1200 (negative scale), FUNCTION ABS(N1 + N2) over an expression argument, and the DISPLAY / MOVE-to-PIC-X / IF-relation / receiver-less channels all render 12.34. It does NOT hold for a floating-point argument: USAGE COMP-1 or COMP-2 is class numeric (8.5.2.12 item 2) and therefore a legal argument-1, but the ABS row is not in the 15.4.1 Float family, so the renderer passes a double into AbsScaled(Int128) and the backend fails with CS1503 -- no value is produced at all. Family-wide pattern, not ABS-only: FUNCTION SIGN and FUNCTION INTEGER over the same COMP-2 item fail identically in one compile. test-needed.

subject: ORD function
notes: Neither half of the rule is enforced: no length check and no category check exists for ORD anywhere on the bind path (BindIntrinsicCore has per-function argument-rule arms for CHAR, DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF, CONVERT, the ALGEBRAIC family... and none for ORD), and IntrinsicCatalog's ArgKinds 's' code is never consulted (IntrinsicSig.ArgKind has zero callers). §15.70.3 r1 plus §4.2.2 para 3 (rules that are 'syntactically distinguishable' shall be indicated by the warning mechanism) require the violation to be flagged; both properties are statically known here — KnownWidth and OperandCategory already exist in this same class and already enforce the IDENTICAL 'shall be one character position in length' phrase for DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF argument-2 via COBOLNET1546 (CheckRepertoireArgs). Concrete failing input, compiled and RUN with the built CLI at --std 2023, zero diagnostics: 01 W3 PIC X(3) VALUE "ABC". 01 NUM PIC 9 VALUE 5. ... MOVE FUNCTION ORD("AB") TO R -> 00066; MOVE FUNCTION ORD(W3) TO R -> 00066 (3 character positions); MOVE FUNCTION ORD(NUM) TO R -> 00054 (category numeric, which the rule excludes). Only the zero-length arm is implemented — CobolIntrinsics.Text.Ord raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION on an empty string citing §15.70.3. Editions: the length constraint applies from the 1989 Intrinsic Function amendment (85) onward; the 'or national' category alternative applies 2002+. test-needed: a negative case rejecting a multi-character and a category-numeric argument-1.

subject: ORD function
notes: Identity PCS: Ord(string) returns s[0] + 1 — the UTF-16 code unit's 0-based position + 1, lowest ordinal 1 (§15.70.1). Non-identity alphanumeric PCS: the binder sets Collate only when ctx.Data.Collating is non-null AND the argument is not national, the renderer appends __COLLATE, and Ord(string, ushort[] weights) returns weights[c] + 1 (Positions[c] is the 0-based collating position, CollatingModel) with c + 1 for a code unit beyond the 256-entry Latin-1 table — correct because all 256 Latin-1 code units occupy positions 0..255, so code unit c >= 256 sits at position c. Goldens verify VALUES: nist IF127A pins FUNCTION ORD("5") = 54 and ORD("A"); conformance 2002/ca26_char_unicode_pcs pins ORD=00257 under ALPHABET AL. Adjacent (NOT this rule): DataBinder.Switches builds the alphanumeric table with 'int code = c & 0xFF', so an ALPHABET literal character above U+00FF aliases to its low byte — a §12.3.7 GR7 k construction defect, not an ORD defect; ORD faithfully reports whatever position the table holds.

subject: ORD function
notes: Class national arrived with COBOL-2002, so r2 applies 2002+. The binder computes nationalArg from OperandCategory and sets CollateNat (never the alphanumeric Collate) for a national argument, so the 256-entry alphanumeric weights table can never alias a national character; with no ALPHABET ... FOR NATIONAL literal phrase the identity body Ord(string) IS the r2 value (D-N3 code-unit order), and under a non-native national sequence Ord(string, NationalCollation) returns NationalCollation.Weight(c) + 1 including the §12.3.7 GR7 k3 arithmetic for unspecified code units. Goldens verify VALUES: conformance 2002/char_national pins ORD(N"世") = 19991 on the native sequence; 2002/alphabet_national pins ORD(N"A") = 00003 and ORD(N" ") = 00036 under ALPHABET REV-NAT FOR NATIONAL IS N"CBA". Premise checked: a NATIONAL GROUP item (the one shape whose category OperandCategory cannot see) is unreachable — GROUP-USAGE appears in no grammar rule, so it is a parse error, not a mis-collated ORD.

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: No argument-class check exists for ORD-MAX anywhere in the binder (only DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF have CheckRepertoireArgs); worse, IsStringOperand AFFIRMATIVELY admits the two shapes the rule bars: it lists `PicCategory.Boolean` and `f.Place.Item.IsGroup` (which includes a strongly-typed group), routing them to OrdMaxString. Verified by compiling and running: `01 B1 PIC 1 USAGE BIT VALUE B"0". 01 B2 PIC 1 USAGE BIT VALUE B"1". ... MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MAX(B1 B2) TO R` compiles silently to `CobolIntrinsics.OrdMaxString(B1, B2)` and displays 0002; and `01 T1 TYPEDEF STRONG. 05 F1 PIC X(3). 01 G1 TYPE T1. 01 G2 TYPE T1. ... MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MAX(G1 G2) TO R` compiles to `OrdMaxString(G1.AsImage(), G2.AsImage())` and displays 0002 — both are §15.71.3 rule 1 violations accepted with no diagnostic. A POINTER argument is not diagnosed either; it escapes as a raw Roslyn error (CS1503 ManagedPointer->Int128) leaking generated-C# detail instead of a §15.71.3 r1 diagnostic. Editions: at --std 85 the barred classes are not declarable (boolean gets COBOLNET0900), so the rule is vacuous there and active 2002+. test-needed (negative cases for boolean, pointer, object, and strongly-typed-group arguments).

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: BindIntrinsicCore has no zero-length-literal guard for ORD-MAX, though the identical rule IS implemented for its siblings (BindConvert checks `BoundStringLiteral { Value.Length: 0 }` for §15.19.3 SR1, CheckRepertoireArgs for §15.66.3 r3) — one rule written in some places and not others. Verified: `MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MAX("" "A") TO R` compiles to `CobolIntrinsics.OrdMaxString("", "A")` and displays 0002 with no diagnostic, at --std 2023, 2014 and 85 alike. Editions recorded as the widest window because I could not establish the edition in which zero-length literals were introduced (§8.3.3/§8.5.4 define them, but Annex E lists no such change) — and the compiler accepts `""` at every --std regardless. test-needed.

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: The binder's category-polymorphic dispatch `if (sig.ArgKinds == "p" && args.Count > 0 && args.All(IsStringOperand))` treats a MIXED argument list not as an error but as the numeric form: any non-string argument silently demotes the whole call to CobolIntrinsics.OrdMax(Int128...) and each alphanumeric argument is coerced through CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric. No diagnostic is issued and no §15.71.3 r3 check exists anywhere (grep for 'same class' finds only ConcatFolder's §8.8.3.2 SR1). Verified: `01 N1 PIC 9(4) VALUE 5. 01 A1 PIC X(4) VALUE "ABCD". ... MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MAX(N1 A1) TO R` compiles to `OrdMax(N1, CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric(A1))` and displays 0001. IsStringOperand also lumps class national together with class alphanumeric, so a national+alphanumeric list — likewise barred by r3, since only alphabetic/alphanumeric mixing is excepted — is silently accepted through OrdMaxString. test-needed.

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: The 1-based ordinal is correct for fixed-point numeric arguments (OrdMax over scale-aligned Int128) and for string arguments (OrdMaxString = ExtremeIndex + 1), verified by running the compiler. But a FLOATING-POINT argument — legal COBOL, since §15.71.3 r1 bars only boolean/message-tag/object/pointer/strongly-typed-group — produces NO value at all: the renderer's `OrdMax or OrdMin` case calls AlignedArgs, which discards the AnyReal flag that AlignedArgsEx computes, and emits `CobolNum.Rescale(CobolFloat.Sending((double)F), 0, 2, ...)` into a `params Int128[]` slot. Concrete failing input: `01 F1 USAGE COMP-2. 01 F2 USAGE COMP-2. 01 R PIC 9(4). ... MOVE 1.5 TO F1 MOVE 2.5 TO F2 MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MAX(F1 F2) TO R` -> 'error: backend compilation failed ... CS1503: cannot convert from double to System.Int128'. Sibling sweep: the same AlignedArgs path is shared by MaxScaled/MinScaled/SumScaled/RangeScaled/MedianScaled/MidrangeScaled, and FUNCTION MAX(F1 F2) fails identically — this is a family-wide defect, not an ORD-MAX one.

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: Both comparison bodies were read and match §8.8.4.2. Numeric path: the renderer aligns every argument to the common scale before the Int128 compare, so unscaled comparison IS algebraic-value comparison (§8.8.4.1.1/§8.8.4.2.3) — verified with mixed-scale operands (-1.05 vs -1.5 vs -1.05 -> 1). String path: CobolString.Compare pads the shorter operand with spaces (§8.8.4.2.7 rule 2 — verified, ORD-MAX("A" "A ") -> 1) and weighs through the alphanumeric PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (ushort[] overload) or the national sequence (NationalCollation overload) per §8.8.4.2.9, wired by the binder's maxMinStr/collate/collateNat flags and the renderer's CollatePrefix — never string.CompareOrdinal. The float-operand shape never reaches the comparison at all; that defect is recorded once, under RV-15.71.4-1. Test gap: nist:IF128A covers numeric and alphanumeric comparison but NOT the collating-sequence leg for ORD-MAX — tests/conformance/2002/intrinsic_max_collating.cob names ORD-MAX only in its comment and calls FUNCTION MAX alone, so it does not cover this rule.

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: Both selection loops use a STRICTLY-greater update, so an argument equal to the running maximum never displaces it and the leftmost position is returned: OrdMax does `if (xs[i] > m)` and ExtremeIndex does `if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0)`. Verified by running the compiler: ORD-MAX(-1.05 -1.5 -1.05) -> 1, ORD-MAX("BB" "AA" "BB") -> 1, and ORD-MAX over a 4-element table holding 3,9,1,9 -> 2. nist:IF128A also exercises ties (FUNCTION ORD-MAX(1, 1)).

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: No argument-class screen exists for ORD-MIN: BindIntrinsicCore runs the §15.66.3/§15.19.3 style check only for DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF/CONVERT, and IsStringOperand EXPLICITLY admits PicCategory.Boolean and IsGroup, so a class-boolean argument and a strongly-typed group argument route to OrdMinString and return a value. Verified at --std 2002/2014/2023: '01 B1 PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT VALUE B"1010". 01 B2 PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT VALUE B"0011". ... MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MIN(B1 B2) TO R' compiles clean and prints 2; the same holds for two '01 G1 TYPE T1.' items where T1 is 'TYPEDEF STRONG'. A USAGE POINTER argument is not diagnosed either — it escapes to the backend as raw Roslyn CS1503 ('cannot convert from ManagedPointer to System.Int128'), a C# error rather than a COBOL diagnostic. At --std 85 the rule is vacuous (boolean/pointer/object/TYPEDEF STRONG are edition-gated by COBOLNET0900); message-tag is a 2023 MCS class with no data-model support, so the reachable divergence is 2002/2014/2023. No fix-queue item owns this yet — the queue is CLOSED at DA7; proposed new item DA8 (one §15 argument-class screen shared by ORD-MIN/ORD-MAX/MAX/MIN, the ArgKinds 'p' rows). test-needed: a negative fixture per barred class at all four editions.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: The zero-length-literal guard exists for FUNCTION NATIONAL-OF (§15.66.3 r3, COBOLNET1546 in CheckRepertoireArgs) and FUNCTION CONVERT (§15.19.3 SR1, COBOLNET1514 in BindConvert) but NOT for ORD-MIN, and there is no shared screen. Verified: 'MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MIN("" "A" "B") TO R' compiles clean and returns 1 at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023, where §15.72.3 rule 2 bars a zero-length literal argument. Editions given as all four because I could not establish from the 2023 text alone which edition first admitted a zero-length literal (§8.3.3.2); the compiler accepts the construct at every edition regardless. Proposed fix-queue item DA8 (see AR-15.72.3-1). test-needed: conformance/negative fixture.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: The binder's only class logic for an ArgKinds 'p' row is 'args.All(IsStringOperand)', which SELECTS the string-vs-numeric runtime body rather than VALIDATING that the arguments share a class, so a mixed-class list is silently accepted. Verified at --std 2023: with '01 N1 PIC 9(4) VALUE 7.' and '01 A1 PIC X(4) VALUE "0003".', 'MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MIN(N1 A1) TO R' compiles clean and returns 2 — the alphanumeric operand is coerced through CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric on the numeric path, comparing 7 against 3. Class national mixed with class alphanumeric is likewise accepted ('01 NA PIC N(3)' + '01 AN PIC X(3)' returns 2). §15.72.3 rule 3 permits ONLY the alphabetic/alphanumeric mixture, and that permitted mixture IS accepted (PIC A(3) + PIC X(3) works — no false rejection). Proposed fix-queue item DA8 (see AR-15.72.3-1). test-needed: conformance/negative fixtures for numeric+alphanumeric and national+alphanumeric, plus a positive fixture pinning the alphabetic/alphanumeric mixture.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: Correct for fixed-point numeric, alphanumeric, national and group arguments (1-based ordinal; verified ORD-MIN(5 2 9 2 1 1)=5, ORD-MIN(0.001 0.0001 1)=2, ORD-MIN("BB" "AA" "AA")=2, plus NIST IF129A's ALL-subscript and nested-call cases). It does NOT hold for FLOATING-POINT arguments, which §15.72.3 does not bar (a FLOAT-LONG item is class numeric): AlignedArgs renders a Real NumX as a bare C# double and feeds it to OrdMin(params Int128[]), so '01 F1 USAGE FLOAT-LONG. 01 F2 USAGE FLOAT-LONG. ... MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MIN(F1 F2) TO R' fails with raw Roslyn 'error CS1503: cannot convert from double to System.Int128' — no value and no COBOL diagnostic. Same for COMP-1/COMP-2, and the defect is family-wide (ORD-MAX, MAX, MIN reproduce it). Proposed fix-queue item DA9 (a float leg for the Int128 variadic statistical family). No fix-queue item owns it yet.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: The comparison follows §8.8.4.2 on every path that emits one: fixed-point numeric arguments are scale-ALIGNED before the unscaled Int128 compare (alignment makes unscaled comparison equal algebraic comparison, §8.8.1); string arguments go through CobolString.Compare, which space-pads the shorter operand (§8.8.4.2.7 r2 — verified ORD-MIN("A" "A ")=1) and honours the alphanumeric PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (verified: under ALPHABET REVSEQ with Z lowest, ORD-MIN("A" "Z")=2 and the program's own IF "Z" < "A" is TRUE — they agree) or the national PCS. PARTIAL for the SAME float shape as RV-15.72.4-1: a FLOAT-LONG/COMP-1/COMP-2 argument list never reaches a comparison at all, because the emitted C# does not compile (CS1503 double -> Int128). Also no test covers the ORD-MIN PCS leg specifically — tests/conformance/2002/intrinsic_max_collating.cob names ORD-MIN in its header comment but exercises only FUNCTION MAX, so it was deliberately NOT cited here.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: Both selection bodies update only on a STRICTLY-less comparison (OrdMin: 'if (xs[i] < m)'; ExtremeIndex: 'if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0)'), so an equal value never displaces an earlier one and the leftmost position wins. Verified: ORD-MIN(5 2 9 2 1 1)=5, ORD-MIN(3 3 3)=1, ORD-MIN(-1 0 -1)=1, ORD-MIN("BB" "AA" "AA")=2, ORD-MIN("A" "A ")=1 (equal after space padding); NIST IF129A test (j) FUNCTION ORD-MIN(A, 5, 5, A) expects 1.

subject: PI function
notes: CobolIntrinsics.Pi() = Math.PI is a legitimate implementor-defined approximation of (3 + 0.1415926535897932384626433832795), and the documentation obligation is met: Annex A.1 item 92 makes the native-arithmetic returned VALUE exempt from documentation while requiring the characteristics/representation, which are documented in CONFORMANCE.md SS7 (the '- (SS15.4.1 / SS14.9.11.4 GR1)' row). PARTIAL for a receiver-shape leg: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat quantizes through FromDouble at ws = max(Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble's scaled double exceeds Int64 at scale >= 19 and SATURATES to long.MaxValue with no size error and no diagnostic. Verified on the built CLI at --std 2023: '01 R19 PIC 9V9(19). COMPUTE R19 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R19.' prints 0.9223372036854775807, and PIC 9V9(30) prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807 - neither is an approximation of pi, so rule 1 is violated for legal 2002+ receivers of 20..31 digits. Not PI-specific: the whole SS15.4.1 float family funnels through the same FromDouble. Test-needed for the scale>=19 leg.

subject: PI function
notes: The rule's precondition can never hold: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is rejected at bind time with COBOLNET0806 (DataBinder.BindDeclarations), an already-ratified documented non-support recorded in CONFORMANCE.md SS2 row 2 ('Not claimed - obsolete feature') and licensed by ISO Annex A.3 item 2 ('The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor', NOTE 1 obsolete). No code computes the exact binary128 value 16312081666030376401667486162748272 / 2**112, and none can while the mode is refused. BARE QUESTION: should SS15.73.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing A.3 item-2 documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? (Recording DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT is an owner decision, so the verdict is parked here.)

subject: PI function
notes: Under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL SS15.73.3 rule 3 requires the returned value to be EXACTLY 3.141592653589793238462643383279503 (the 34-digit SS8.8.1.5 standard-decimal intermediate); SS15.4.1's last paragraph ('unless otherwise specified in the function definition') is exactly what rule 3 does, so the standard-arithmetic staging premise written in CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs and in IntrinsicBinder's staging comment - 'the prose-approximation functions ... are implementor-defined in EVERY mode' - is FALSE for PI. PI is absent from the IntrinsicBinder staged-loud list (ANNUITY/PRESENT-VALUE/VARIANCE/STANDARD-DEVIATION) and rides the ordinary RenderFloat/Math.PI/binary64 path in every arithmetic mode, so a STANDARD-DECIMAL program silently gets native binary64 digits. FAILING INPUT (verified on the built CLI at --std 2023): IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. PISDCK2. OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 R17 PIC 9V9(17). PROCEDURE DIVISION. COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R17. -- prints 3.14159265358979328, the spec requires 3.14159265358979324 (rule 3 truncated to the receiver). At PIC 9V9(30) it prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807 (the FromDouble Int64 saturation) against a required 3.141592653589793238462643383279. Test-needed. Sibling: FUNCTION E (SS15.27.3) carries the same three-mode returned-value structure and the same defect.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: test-needed. §15.74.3 r1 (cite.py --check: OK) — argument-1 and argument-2 shall be of the class numeric; §15.3 argument type 10 reads 'An arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified'. NOTHING enforces it for PRESENT-VALUE. IntrinsicSig.ArgKind(int) has ZERO call sites across src/Cobol.Net.* (the only ArgKinds read anywhere is the `sig.ArgKinds == "p"` MAX/MIN test), and BindArgOperand routes every argument through ExpressionBinder with OperandContext.FunctionArgument, whose OperandRef gate is `context is OperandContext.Arithmetic && NonNumericOperandKind(p) is { }` — deliberately skipped for function arguments because 'the function's own §15.x argument rule governs' — and PRESENT-VALUE has no such per-function rule (unlike CHAR/COBOLNET0844, DISPLAY-OF+NATIONAL-OF/CheckRepertoireArgs, the ALGEBRAIC family/AlgebraicArgError). TWO shapes reproduced with the built CLI, no diagnostic at --std 85, 2002, 2014 or 2023: (a) data item — `01 ALPHA-ARG PIC X(5) VALUE "ABCDE". 01 AMT PIC 9(5)V99 VALUE 1000.00. COMPUTE RESULT-X = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(ALPHA-ARG AMT)` prints 1000.0000 (ALPHA-ARG decoded through CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric as an unsigned integer, giving rate 0); (b) alphanumeric LITERAL — `COMPUTE RESULT-X = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE("ABC" 100)` prints 100.000000. Required: reject both at bind time. Fix shape (rule 5): drive the check off IntrinsicSig.ArgKinds at the one BindIntrinsicCore chokepoint rather than adding a tenth hand-written per-function one-off — ArgKind() is dead for EVERY intrinsic, so the per-position class column of the catalog is currently decorative compiler-wide.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: test-needed. §15.74.3 r2 (cite.py --check: OK) — the value of argument-1 shall be greater than −1. This is a permissible-VALUE constraint, so §15.3 applies: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument … the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist'; Annex A.1 item 90 makes only the RETURNED VALUE implementor-defined when checking is off — the condition must still be SET, and must be raised when checking is on. CobolIntrinsics.PresentValue(double rate, params double[] amounts) performs no domain check on rate, unlike its file-mates Log/Log10 which call Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError, and the binder adds none. Reproduced with the built CLI: (a) COMPILE-TIME-detectable literal violation, edition-independent — `COMPUTE RESULT-X = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(-1.5, 100, 200)` is accepted silently at --std 85 AND --std 2023 and prints 600.000000, so the divergence does not depend on the (2002+) EC machinery and holds at every edition; (b) runtime rate with checking explicitly enabled — `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` then `FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(R2 AMT AMT)` with R2 = −2.00 prints 0 and CONTINUES, while the very next `FUNCTION LOG(0)` in the SAME program aborts with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal)' — same directive, same run unit, so the mechanism exists and PRESENT-VALUE alone does not use it; (c) rate = −1.00 exactly makes 1+rate = 0, and the binary64 division through FromDouble SATURATES, printing 223372036.8547 with no exception and no diagnostic.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: Holds under NATIVE arithmetic; the standard-arithmetic leg does not. The body `for (int i = 0; i < amounts.Length; i++) pv += amounts[i] / Math.Pow(1 + rate, i + 1)` is exactly Σ argument-2ᵢ / (1 + argument-1)^i for i = 1..n — §15.74.4 r1c, with r1a and r1b as its n = 1 and n = 2 cases — and §15.4.1 licenses 'an implementor-defined approximation' under native arithmetic. Verified with the built CLI: PRESENT-VALUE(0.100 1000 2000 3000) and the hand-written FUNCTION SUM EAE both give 4815.927873, which is also the exact hand-computed value. Annex A.1 item 92 ('Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic) … The value returned does not have to be documented') means the documentation test does NOT downgrade the native leg, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md already carries a §15.4.1 / §14.9.11.4 GR1 row. THE PARTIAL: §15.4.1 r1 requires the returned value to EQUAL the equivalent arithmetic expression when standard-decimal OR STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic is in effect, and instead of doing so IntrinsicBinder rejects the program with DiagnosticCatalog.ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic (COBOLNET0899, EditionSeverity.Error) — legal COBOL refused; confirmed by running an OPTIONS/ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL program. ⚠ NOTE FOR THE FIX SESSION: that staging condition is `ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.Standard or ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal` and OMITS ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary, which §15.4.1 covers equally. I checked whether that opens a SILENT-wrong-answer hole and it does not — today ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is itself loud-rejected earlier by COBOLNET0806 ('obsolete feature … not supported') at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, so standard-binary can never be in effect — but if 0806 is ever lifted (obsolete is not removed; §11.9.5 still defines the phrase in 2023), the 0899 list must gain StandardBinary or PRESENT-VALUE will silently return the native double. The rule itself applies at all four editions; the failing leg needs the OPTIONS ARITHMETIC clause and so is reachable only from 2002. ⚠ TEST-REF CORRECTED: nist:IF403M was STRUCK on two independent grounds — it is registered 'pending / none / cataloged (not asserted)' in tests/nist/corpus.tsv line 406 so nothing runs it, and its sole PRESENT-VALUE statement compares the function to ITSELF (`IF FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE (0, 23, 12, 9) = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE (0, 23, 12, 9)`), which tests determinism, never the equivalent arithmetic expression. nist:IF130A genuinely covers the native leg — F-PRES-VAL-01 range-checks PRESENT-VALUE(0, 23, 12, 9) against 43.9991..44.0009 and twenty-one further paragraphs range-check real values. No test covers the standard-decimal leg (tests/conformance/negative/arith-standard-intrinsic-staged.cob exercises VARIANCE, not PRESENT-VALUE, so it is deliberately not cited).

subject: RANDOM function
notes: No class-numeric check is ever performed on a RANDOM argument: IntrinsicSig.ArgKind is DEFINED in IntrinsicCatalog.cs but has NO call site anywhere in src/Cobol.Net.* (the only ArgKinds read is the 'p' MAX/MIN polymorphism test in BindIntrinsicCore), and BindArgOperand routes through BindFunctionArgumentExpr, which by design suppresses the OperandContext.Arithmetic non-numeric screen (ExpressionBinder.OperandRef / COBOLNET0844). Per 15.75.3 rule 1 with the 15.3 type-10 definition ('Numeric. An arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified') a class-alphanumeric operand is illegal. subject: RANDOM function
notes: Random(long seed) REPLACES the one static _random with a freshly seeded generator, so a subsequent seeded reference restarts the sequence. Verified: FUNCTION RANDOM(42) -> 0.668106466, argument-less -> 0.140907298, FUNCTION RANDOM(42) again -> 0.668106466 (identical). subject: RANDOM function
notes: The determination exists in code: the field initializer `private static Random _random = new()` -- the parameterless .NET seed, i.e. an entropy-derived per-process value, used when the first reference in the run unit carries no argument-1. Annex A.1 item 144 makes this a REQUIRED implementor-defined item but explicitly WAIVES documentation ('The seed value used by the implementor does not have to be documented'), so the absent CONFORMANCE.md entry is not a conformance defect here. Observation for the owner, not a defect: the default seed VARIES per run (three consecutive runs gave first values 0.377486289 / 0.408692634 / 0.927035267), so an un-seeded sequence is not reproducible, unlike GnuCOBOL/IBM/Micro Focus which pin a fixed default seed. NIST IF131A F-RANDOM-01 is the first RANDOM reference in that run unit and is argument-less, so it exercises this path.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: The zero-argument overload `public static double Random() => _random.NextDouble()` advances the ONE current sequence; IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat routes `"Random" when ic.Args.Count == 0` to it with an empty argument list. One static per run unit (the Runtime assembly is shared by every compilation unit of the run unit), matching the rule's run-unit scope. Verified: after seed 42, successive argument-less references gave 0.140907298 then 0.125518289 (progressing, never restarting).

subject: RANDOM function
notes: The runtime body conforms (Random.NextDouble() is in [0,1)) and the FLOAT-receiver path (num.Receiver.Real) hands that double through unquantized. The FIXED-POINT receiver path does not: RenderFloat wraps the call in FromDouble(call, ws) with ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble ends in `(long)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`. .NET's SEEDED Random is the legacy compat generator whose NextDouble() is InternalSample() * (1.0/int.MaxValue), whose maximum value is 2147483646/2147483647 = 0.99999999953433871; at ws = 9 that scales to 999999999.534 and rounds AWAY FROM ZERO to 1000000000, i.e. the function result is exactly 1.000000000 -- not 'less than one'. One draw in 2^31 (~4.7e-10) hits it, so I could not exhibit a deterministic failing COBOL input within this session's budget; the defect is read off the code path, not conjectured. Fix shape: clamp at the quantization point (or round toward zero for RANDOM) rather than leaving the bound to the emitter's generic float rounding.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: Random(long seed) constructs `new Random(int)`, whose seeded implementation is .NET's pinned back-compatible (Knuth subtractive) generator -- deterministic for a given seed. Verified BOTH within a process (FUNCTION RANDOM(42) twice, separated by argument-less draws, gives 0.668106466 both times) and ACROSS processes (two separate runs of the same program produced byte-identical output: 0668106466 / 0140907298 / 0125518289 / 0668106466).

subject: RANDOM function
notes: The BEHAVIOUR meets the numeric floor: `new Random((int)(seed & 0x7FFFFFFF))` is the identity on 0..2147483647, so every seed in 0..32767 gets a distinct generator state and hence a distinct sequence (spot-checked: seed 0 -> 0.726243270, seed 32767 -> 0.036513305). Seeds at or above 2^31 alias downward -- verified FUNCTION RANDOM(2147483648) == FUNCTION RANDOM(0) and FUNCTION RANDOM(2147483649) == FUNCTION RANDOM(1) -- which is legitimate latitude precisely BECAUSE rule 3 lets the implementor specify the subset. But rule 3's obligation is to SPECIFY that subset, and Annex A.1 item 145 makes it a required item that 'shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation'. Documented in CONFORMANCE.md section 7: NO -- section 7 currently carries only items 2, 59, 158 and 205-215. Conforming requires the entry as well as the behaviour, so this is PARTIAL until CONFORMANCE.md section 7 states the subset (0..2147483647, aliasing modulo 2^31 above that). test-needed (no test asserts that two distinct seeds in 0..32767 yield distinct sequences).

Nothing else re-checks class, so §15.76.3 rule 1 ("Argument-1 shall be of class numeric"; §15.3 type 10 = "an arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified") is silently unenforced and the alphanumeric image is digit-decoded by NumericRenderer.FieldNumCore. Verified on the built CLI at --std 2023 AND --std 85 (strict, no --permissive): 01 A-TXT PIC X(3) VALUE "012". 01 B-TXT PIC X(3) VALUE "345". COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANGE(A-TXT B-TXT) compiles with no diagnostic and prints R=00333. Same silent acceptance for an alphanumeric literal (FUNCTION RANGE("99" 5) -> 94), a GROUP item, a PIC N national item, and a numeric-EDITED item (PIC ZZ9.99, class alphanumeric per the §8.4.2 class/category table) -- and note the group case is the exact shape strict conformance already rejects in an arithmetic expression, so the two contexts disagree. test-needed: a tests/conformance/negative case pinning a non-numeric RANGE argument at all four editions (the existing da6-*-numeric-operand negatives cover §8.8.1.1 arithmetic operands only, not the §15 function-argument context).

subject: RANGE function
notes: The runtime body IS the equivalent arithmetic expression, literally: RangeScaled(params Int128[] xs) => MaxScaled(xs) - MinScaled(xs), over arguments the emitter has aligned to their common scale via AlignedArgs (so unscaled compare/subtract == algebraic compare/subtract, §8.8.1), result returned at that common scale. Empirically verified against the spec's own EAE written out longhand: FUNCTION RANGE(N1 N2 7) and FUNCTION MAX(N1 N2 7) - FUNCTION MIN(N1 N2 7) both give 52.50 for N1=-12.5 N2=40; the one-argument case gives 0; a mixed-scale table(ALL) gives 13.50 for {1.25,-3.5,10.0,0.75}. Exact in Int128 -- no rounding decision is buried in the subtraction -- and the family header derives why the same holds under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD/STANDARD-DECIMAL (a compare and a subtract are exact in a 34-digit SDIDI too), which is why RANGE is correctly absent from the IntrinsicBinder standard-arithmetic loud-stage list.

subject: REM function
notes: Both §15.3 legs verified by execution. RemScaled tests b == 0 on the SCALE-ALIGNED divisor (Align only ever scales UP to max(a.Scale,b.Scale), so no truncation can manufacture or hide a zero) and calls ExceptionState.ArgumentError: with >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON the run unit terminates with "EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): REM with a zero divisor (15.77.3 rule 2)"; with checking off the §15.3 implementor-defined default 0 is returned, for both a literal 0 and a zero-valued item. test-needed: no test exercises REM's zero divisor — the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION tests (ExceptionConditionConformanceTests, IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.OutOfDomain_EcDefaultZero_PinnedToSpec) use LOG/NUMVAL/SQRT/FACTORIAL, and no NIST REM case (IF133A, IF403M) passes a zero argument-2. Separately noted for the §15.3 inventory row, not this one: the implementor-defined default result 0 has no entry in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7.

subject: REM function
notes: The equivalent arithmetic expression is realized EXACTLY for fixed-point operands: the emitter aligns both arguments to s = max(scaleA, scaleB) and RemScaled returns a % b at scale s, and since Int128 % truncates toward zero it IS FUNCTION INTEGER-PART of the quotient — algebraically (a_u - b_u*trunc(a_u/b_u))/10^s = argument-1 - argument-2 * INTEGER-PART(argument-1/argument-2). Verified by execution: REM(-11,5)=-1, REM(11,-5)=1, REM(11.5,2.25)=0.25. But NO returned value is produced at all for two operand shapes §15.3 item 10 explicitly permits, at every edition: (a) a FLOAT operand (USAGE COMP-2 / COMP-1 — category numeric per §8.5.2.12 item 2) renders as a C# double that the emitter hands straight to RemScaled(Int128,Int128) -> backend failure `CS1503: cannot convert from 'double' to 'System.Int128'`; (b) under OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL an arithmetic-expression argument renders as CobolDec -> `CS1503: cannot convert from 'CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDec' to 'System.Int128'`. Failing input (a): 01 F1 USAGE COMP-2. 01 F2 USAGE COMP-2. 01 R PIC S9(5)V99. ... MOVE 11.5 TO F1. MOVE 2.25 TO F2. COMPUTE R = FUNCTION REM(F1, F2). Failing input (b): OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. ... 01 A PIC S9(4) VALUE 17. 01 B PIC S9(4) VALUE 5. ... COMPUTE R = FUNCTION REM(A + 3, B). This is a FAMILY defect, not a REM defect: the same Arg/AlignedArgs -> Int128 runtime signature path breaks FUNCTION MAX/ABS/SUM (and MOD, MIN, RANGE, MEDIAN, MIDRANGE, ORD-MAX/MIN, INTEGER, INTEGER-PART, FRACTION-PART) on the identical inputs — verified for MAX/ABS/SUM with COMP-2 operands in one program, three CS1503 sites.

subject: REVERSE function
notes: CobolIntrinsics.Reverse is an exact position-j <- position-(n-j+1) code-unit reversal with no length change, and the argument reaches it as the operand's FULL fixed-width image (OperandText.AsString), so n is the declared size, not the trimmed value. Verified by running the built CLI: X(6) VALUE "AB" -> [    BA  ] into X(8); ref-mod W-S(2:3) -> [  B     ]; A(5) "ABCDE" -> [EDCBA   ]; N(5) N"ABCDE" -> [EDCBA   ] with the result category correctly resolved to National (the CA25 arm in IntrinsicBinder). Surrogate/composite sequences need no special handling: ISO 8.5.1.4 item 2 and its closing paragraph make each two-octet UTF-16 code element its own character position, which is exactly the code-unit reversal implemented.

(BoundStringLiteral carries Category=Boolean), but its content can never tokenize as a §15.3 format, so it resolves to EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION — verified fatal under >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON — which §15.3 last paragraph and A.1 item 90 make a conforming disposition of an argument-rule violation. test-needed: the shared COBOLNET1517 arm is covered only for FORMATTED-DATE (conformance-test:IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.FormattedDate_NonLiteralFormat_1517); the SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME leg has no test. FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYMMDD", "20210616") compiles clean and returns 0 with no diagnostic and no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION even under >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON (verified). subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: Analyze walks argument-2 segment by segment against the tokenized format, checking every data-bearing separator (colon, decimal separator, T, W, Z, offset sign), digit-only content, per-subfield ranges from §15.3.3.3 / §15.3.3.6.2 (hh 00-23, mm 00-59, ss 00-59 under the LEAP-SECOND OFF default, offset hours 00-23 / minutes 00-59, zero-sign forcing zero magnitude per §15.3.3.6.1), short data and trailing data; a nonzero result routes to ArgumentError, which sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns the §15.3 implementor-defined default 0. Verified: "256100"/'hhmmss' -> 0, and fatal EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION under >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON; "12-34-56"/'hh:mm:ss' -> 0; "1234"/'hhmmss' -> 0. test-needed: no test exercises an invalid argument-2 for this function.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: For a combined date and time format the SAME Analyze pass validates the date portion (year > 1600 per §15.3.1.3, month 01-12, day-of-month against DaysInMonth of the analyzed year/month, day-of-year against the leap-year length, ISO week 01-52/53 via LongIsoYear, day-of-week 1-7) as well as the mandatory 'T' in the data (§15.3.3.7) — and, per D.31.5.9, the date is validated but does NOT enter the returned value. Verified: FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500") -> 18867.81 (the D.31.5.9 worked example), while the same format with "19950231T05142781+0500" (Feb 31) yields the §15.3 default 0. test-needed: no test exercises a combined format with an invalid date for this function.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: ((H*3600)+(M*60)+S) is computed exactly for fraction widths up to NINE digits — Analyze forms ((long)hh*3600 + mi*60 + ss) * 10^f + frac at scale f, S correctly carrying the fractional-second digits of the seconds subfield (§15.3.3.2), and the offset/UTC subfields correctly NOT entering the sum; both D.31.5.9 worked examples reproduce exactly ("hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" -> 18867.81). It breaks at TEN or more fractional-second digits: Analyze accumulates every subfield into a local `int val`, so the fraction wraps at 2^31 in unchecked arithmetic. FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss.ssssssssss", "1234563000000000") returns 45295.8705032704 instead of 45296.3000000000 (3000000000 - 2^32 = -1294967296), and with twelve digits "hhmmss.ssssssssssss"/"123456812479168304" returns 45296.000730349360 instead of 45296.812479168304. §15.3.3.2 makes the maximum fraction width implementor-defined with a floor of nine; COBOL.NET neither enforces nor documents a maximum — A.1 item 202 ('Time formats and corresponding function values (maximum precision not less than nine fractional digits)', required and 'shall be documented') is documented in CONFORMANCE.md §7: NO — so a >9-digit format is accepted and silently yields a wrong value. The two existing tests only exercise 0 and 2 fraction digits, so nothing covers the overflow.

notes: Independently re-verified, not inherited. §15.74.2 validated with cite.py, and the TRANSCRIPTION checked against the canonical PDF (page 934 = printed folio 904, text extracted from specs-private/): the printed diagram reads 'FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE ( argument-1 { argument-2 }  ...  )' with FUNCTION and PRESENT-VALUE the only underlined words — no OCR loss, no falsely-restrictive residue. Per §5.2 (spec line 2379) the ellipsis repeats the portion between the matching brace pair, and a single-alternative brace is required, so argument-2 shall appear at least once: minimum 2 arguments, no maximum.
